children: , the social-media and digital-advertising giant, faced a fresh regulatory challenge Tuesday as Australia unveiled its draft Digital Duty of Care. The shares were nearly flat, slipping a bit to $616.68 during early trading.

Australia's My Feed, My Way proposal would force social platforms to tell users how recommendations work and offer a feed showing only accounts they deliberately follow. Violations could trigger penalties of A$109.2 million, or roughly $79 million. The plan must still clear consultation before reaching Parliament, but the direction is clear: Australia wants algorithms to become a choice, not a default.

Meta produced $60.80 billion in second-quarter revenue, powered by a 14% increase in ad impressions and a 12% jump in average ad prices. The maximum fine equals only about 0.13% of that quarterly haul, so the financial sting looks small. title: Meta Slips as Australia Offers an Algorithm Escape Hatch
